input.quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise; provided that the acquiring party agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 18.9 is mutual and already delivers most of the fallback: either Party may assign to an acquirer of substantially all of its business or assets without consent, on a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party, and all other assignments require the other Party's written consent (the Affiliate route in the second paragraph also requires prior written consent, so it does not undercut the consent requirement). The fallback fails on one material term: consent to non-successor assignments is at the other Party's unfettered discretion, with no reasonableness standard — even though the same Section applies a "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed" standard to Affiliate assignments. We therefore add that qualifier to the general consent requirement, taking the clause to the fallback rather than rewriting it to the asymmetric preferred position. No change-of-control exit exists against us: Section 18.10 and Section 4.5(b) address only a Change in Control of Array (firewalls and the lapse of a combination-study restriction), and no provision gives Array a termination or re-pricing right on an Ono Change in Control.

proposal.summary: Add a reasonableness standard to the consent required for non-successor assignments under Section 18.9.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 18.9 already lets either Party assign to an acquirer of substantially all of its business or assets on a writing delivered to the other Party, but consent for any other assignment is at the other Party's absolute discretion. We have added the customary reasonableness qualifier, consistent with the standard already used for Affiliate assignments in the same Section.
